standard_prerequisites.name: Embedding
standard_prerequisites.statement: A map f : X to Y is an embedding when for all x, x prime the action on paths ap(f) is an equivalence of the path types.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the hypothesis on the map.

standard_prerequisites.name: n-type
standard_prerequisites.statement: Y is an n-type when its path types are (n minus one)-types, with the level shifted down once per path iteration.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the level hypothesis on the codomain and the conclusion for the domain.

standard_prerequisites.name: Level of an equivalent type
standard_prerequisites.statement: A type equivalent to an (n minus one)-type is again an (n minus one)-type.
standard_prerequisites.use: It transfers the level from the path type in Y to the path type in X.

core_obligations: Fix x and x prime in X and reduce the goal to showing that the path type of X is an (n minus one)-type (source lines 107-107).
Use that f is an embedding to get an equivalence between the path types of X and those of Y at the images (source lines 108-108).
Transfer the level along that equivalence, since the path type of Y is an (n minus one)-type by the hypothesis that Y is an n-type (source lines 108-109).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce to the level of a single path type.
Use the embedding equivalence and the level hypothesis on Y.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled theorem at source lines 102-105 (book Theorem 7.1.6): if f : X to Y is an embedding and Y is an n-type for some n at least minus one, then X is an n-type. The statement is a level transfer with no argument, and the proof (source lines 106-109) has to notice that the level of a type is decided one path type at a time, that the embedding hypothesis supplies an equivalence between the path type of X at a pair and the path type of Y at the images, and that a level is preserved by equivalence; the shift of the level by one between the statement and the goal is exactly where the bookkeeping sits.
